18th May 2556, 1106 hours

Kriegsmark, Bridge

"What's that?" Stan said with his voice as high as it would go without yelling, "you gotta speak up or into the mic."

Aftward in the ship the roaring vertical thrusters making everything vibrate uncomfortably and loudly. He loved it. Over in the co-pilot's seat Inzili with her claws tight in her lap, she truly hated flying and especially in something so old cobbled together with even older parts. Meanwhile Stan had a single hand on the control wheel and a second on the many levers of the throttle system, the four short and stubby ones pushed mostly forward to make the craft rise in the air. For their short hop to the village he would be using them for primary lift, for practical reasons, but he didn't mind the extra work.

Jade put on her headset and turned on the microphone, "nothing important, Inzili don't you think it would be time to get Jhoka?"

Inzili didn't reply, her figure tense as she tried her best to trust Stan's abilities as the nose of the ship lifted slightly before the entire thing raised up slowly into the air.

"Alright, raising gear," Stan muttered, but it was easily picked up over the mic, "fire suppression."

Near the unseen thrusters there was a loud roar that ended a second later and heralded a large white cloud being forced out over the grassy field below.

"And a turn."

While still in a hover the craft banked slightly to starboard as the nose of the craft pointed in the general direction of Jhoka's village. Their maneuver gave Jade a good view of the large scorchmark they had created and the cloud used to extinguish it, she sat up as far as she could to peer out the window with a grin. She liked flying.

"And we're off!"

Four of the larger throttle levers were pushed forward with two smaller thin ones off to the side untouched. These were for low-impulse maneuvering or for quick bursts of speed at full throttle, they controlled a pair of smaller, independent engines each on the lower nacelles. It all happened in an instant, the roar of the engines brought thrust that tried to throw everyone to the rear of the ship. His thumb remained on the levers, but they weren't yet necessary. During the days when the ship was new these smaller engines were often held in reserve until they were absolutely crucial, they quickly required maintenance after even short periods of use and were easy to burn out.

Well the old girl didn't need it, even with half her skin bundled up on top under a tarp.

Stan pushed the craft higher and higher until he was at a reasonable altitude to avoid the trees, flying in the general direction they took when driving to the village. Speed meant stability, so he increased the throttle until they had accelerated fast enough for the smooth underside to generate more lift than the vertical jets; his fiancee huffed as she scurried out of the chair to go fetch Jhoka. Both toddlers were left alone on the jumpseats, the nearby storage compartments locked away to keep their curious hands out, but they were thoroughly distracted by the sensation of flying anyway. Returning with the younger woman Inzili pointed to the moving landscape ahead, the sight of trees under her made the tribal girl gasp loudly in complete awe.

"This... is real," she whispered, looking right into Inzili's eyes. "We're flying! Like birds!"

"Mmm, we are," Inzili giggled, "this is the way back to your village, yes?"

Jhoka didn't immediately respond, she just stared ahead out at the view as the ship glided effortlessly over the trees meters below.

Experiencing flight for the first time was amazing for the young huntress, she looked out across the trees with an open-mouthed, awestruck grin as the forest raced by underneath. They lifted into the air and despite the terrible noise and vibrations she saw further and further as they lifted into the air. Far off in the distance she could see the wide river that she had been ordered to march toward, pulling behind the big water-vine from the ship. At first the why was not clear, Inzili explained it to her during one of their morning bathing sessions and Jhoka felt proud having made the trek for extra water. As the ship turned she saw the faint tracks of the hunting expedition that was done just so she would not return home in shame, and now she was riding on a mighty vessel that would deliver her one last time to her village. Tales would be told for many moons of this day!

Finally exhaling the tension in her chest Jhoka nodded quickly and said, "oh yes, keep going! Straight ahead, you can even see the path I take... there!"

Pressing her nubile body against the back of the chair and resting her petite breasts against the back of the pilot's head she jammed a finger forward toward a small dirt path cutting through the grass beyond the trees. Her claws were on Stan's shoulders as she watched him fly, her excitement bubbling out in a happy giggle. Shaking her head slowly Inzili pulled the younger lizard back by her shoulders.

"Do not bump Teekus, this is dangerous enough as it is," she chided softly with a nervous scowl.

Flight was a wonder to her too once, so very long ago, so she could forgive the girl's enthusiasm for the time being. She understood they weren't really flying, the ship moved much faster when that happened, but at least the vibrations had died down somewhat as they flew.

"See it? Way the hell up there?" Stan called out, pointing toward the horizon.

Thin wisps of smoke marked the location among a sea of green, the fires of many hearths made it so easy to spot from the air.

"This is so exciting!" Jhoka exclaimed, her toe claws chattering against the floor in excitement as she watched them follow the path.

After several minutes, and she knew they were minutes because she could see the clock, her attention shifted to the human who was making all of this happen. Inzili had returned to her seat which left Jhoka standing there, looking down with both curiosity and awe as she watched his hands transition gracefully from one thing to the next, beneath the console she could see his feet dance between four pedals extending from the floor. Such graceful, careful movements controlling something so big made her greatly appreciate his skill the more she watched and sensed. Below her feet she could actually feel his commanding touch, her sense of balance and motion made a ball of excitement twist to life in her chest... but it didn't run away! She had to fight to ride it, to keep from shuddering and crying out from the jubilation, it was a rush just to master her own body as much as it was to actually fly.

Then she looked at him, leaning to see around his head, she saw her own emotions mirrored in a tamed hurricane under his tightly regulated features. He had taught her a word earlier that she forgot, when they were retrieving the cold-making thing from the ruins, it came with a tap to the chest to convey the concept.

"Teekus?" she began, tapping his chest gently, "how say?"

"Huh? Oh, yeah... Excitement. Can you say 'excitement' for me?"

That was it, she grinned and repeated his word into his ear as she withdrew from his sphere of influence. A thumbs up was what she got for her effort, good work, that laconic praise always made her heart flutter. Ahead she saw what looked like a hole in the carpet of leaves, the blackened surface of the mud below was peppered with red figures milling around. Surely they would rush back to their territory with word about the flying monstrosity, but she didn't get to see their animated response and the camp was behind them before she finished the thought.

"Honey, we're gonna have to set down for a bit while longer than I expected," Stan said to the purple tawaunan, a finger tapping the display between them, "gotta check that over."

Jade unbuckled and slipped around the tribal girl to see. "You just keep flying and don't worry, I'll go back there and check the manifold pressure myself."

"Yeah, keep me informed."

Still new to the language, the tribal girl didn't understand the conversation very well, or really at all, but she was confident they had the situation under control so she went back to focusing on the pilot. After several intense minutes of observation she had figured out the most basic controls for the ship, Jhoka was a very, very quick study after all, and surmised that she vaguely understood the controls. At least two of the pedals controlled the side to side movements, the grip in Stan's hand controlled the leaning motion and the upward and downward motion of the front. What she didn't know, and couldn't from her observations, was the extra pair of pedals controlled lateral movement which could push the ship side to side quickly in the current flight mode.

Ahead of him she saw the dancing lights and lines that seemed to indicate, at least the lines did, the orientation of the ship and perhaps some other flight-oriented information that was well beyond her understanding. If it was there it had to have a purpose, everything seemed so... deliberate up in front.
